peggingPanel.title: Pegging:
peggingPanel.info: First level below = direct contributors; their edge qtys sum to Allocated above. Deeper levels: qty = flow along that edge (· = leaf, no further expansion).

basketPanel.titleFinal: Basket at end of loaded view
basketPanel.finalInfo: Final basket after all allocation steps. Consumed supplies are removed.
basketPanel.scarcityInfo: Scarcity = total quantity per component; scarcest first. Basket = initial supplies (minus consumed) + produced in this run. Produced output is added after its step, so it appears at the beginning of the next step.

errors.allocationTimeout: Stopped waiting for allocation (20 min). The run may still be in progress—refresh the page or check the Run list.

planning.info: Demand-to-supply planning: takes customer demands and outputs committed demands (with commit_time) and planned work orders. Use
planning.infoSuffix: to set how methods are chosen (preference cascade, scored elaborate, or equal split), or enable shared-component consolidation.

overridesPanel.title: User overrides
overridesPanel.info: Overrides let you manually control: method selection (make/move/buy) or component split allocation among competing demands. Active overrides are applied on the next plan run.
overridesPanel.noOverrides: No overrides set. Use the "Override" button on a work order in the results table to create one.

config.equalSplitMethods: Equal split across methods (when multiple make/move/buy can fulfill a demand; can be slower—we plan each method branch)
config.elaborateMethod: Use elaborate method selection (slower, scores by commit/inventory/purchase; ignored when equal split across methods is on)
config.depthOptimalHint: Auto-search the best depth: planner runs depth=1, 2, 3 … and stops at the first depth where the weighted plan score (commit / inventory / purchase) does not improve over the previous depth. Capped at 10. Each step costs a full plan, so use sparingly.
config.weightsHint: Relative weights the elaborate scorer applies to commit time / inventory consumed / purchase amount. Backend normalizes so absolute values don't matter — only the ratio.
config.purchaseAllowed: Purchase allowed (uncheck to exclude buy methods from planning)
config.consolidate: Consolidate shared components (group demands within a time bucket into one work order, then split output)
config.resetDefaultsTitle: Reset planning config: method by preference (depth 1), purchase disallowed, consolidation on (365-day bucket, fair split)

peggingPanel.title: Pegging:
peggingPanel.rootInfo: Root = this work order; below it are the supplies that fulfill it (inventory, child work orders, purchase) at all levels.
peggingPanel.legendInfo: ▢ Inventory (static state) and ⚙ Work order (transformation). Root = target inventory; work orders transform between states; leaves = supply or purchase inventory.
peggingPanel.orInfo: When multiple inventories or work orders appear as siblings under the same parent, they are alternative paths
peggingPanel.orInfoSuffix: that can each supply flow to that parent.
peggingPanel.hangInfo: If this hangs: run plan first (backend stores result per case), then open pegging. Check browser console (F12) and backend logs for errors.
peggingPanel.noWoData: No pegging for this work order. Run plan first.
peggingPanel.noDemandPegging: No pegging tree for this demand. Re-run plan to get planning_pegging.
peggingPanel.anyOf: ANY of the inventories / work orders below can supply this node (OR).
peggingPanel.allOf: ALL of the inventories / work orders below are required together (AND).
peggingPanel.noWos: No work orders — planning could not fulfill this demand (no method or child failed).
peggingPanel.noChildren: No component breakdown (leaf work order or depth-limited).

copilot.title: Planning copilot
copilot.naturalLangInfo: Express your requirements in natural language; the system may ask follow-up questions to clarify.
copilot.examplesRest: selection. Examples: "use elaborate method selection", "method depth 2", "equal split across methods", "by preference", "show current config". With an LLM enabled, you can use natural language and the assistant may ask clarifying questions.
copilot.inputPlaceholder: e.g. use elaborate method selection at depth 2

replies.empty: You can configure method selection, purchase, or shared-component consolidation. Say "show config" to see current settings.
replies.methodDepth: Set method elaborate **depth** to {depth}. The planner will score candidate methods at the top {depth} recursion level(s). Re-run plan to apply.
replies.methodDepthOptimal: Enabled **optimal depth search**. The planner will run depth=1, 2, 3 … and stop at the first depth where the weighted plan score (commit / inventory / purchase) does not improve. Capped at 10. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.methodDepthManual: Disabled optimal depth search. The planner will use the fixed depth value. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.methodEqual: Set method selection to **equal split across methods**. When multiple make/move/buy methods can fulfill a demand, quantity is divided equally among them. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.methodElaborate: Set method selection to **elaborate (score by simulation)**. The planner simulates each method's child materials and picks the one with earliest commit, most inventory consumed, and least purchase. Slower. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.methodPreference: Set method selection to **by preference (cascade)**. The planner tries the most preferred method first; if its child materials cannot be planned, it falls back to the next preferred method. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.methodWeightCommit: Set elaborate score weights to favor **earliest delivery** (commit 1, inventory 0, purchase 0). Re-run plan to apply.
replies.methodWeightInventory: Set elaborate score weights to favor **existing inventory** (commit 0, inventory 1, purchase 0). Re-run plan to apply.
replies.methodWeightPurchase: Set elaborate score weights to favor **minimizing additional purchase** (commit 0, inventory 0, purchase 1). Re-run plan to apply.
replies.purchaseOff: Purchase (buy method) **disabled**. The planner will not use buy methods; demands will be fulfilled from inventory, make, or move only. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.purchaseOn: Purchase (buy method) **allowed**. The planner will use buy methods when available. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.consolidationOn: Enabled **shared-component consolidation**. Demands within the same time bucket (currently {days} days) that share a component will be grouped into one work order, then output is split by {mode}. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.consolidationOnModeFair: fair (priority when ample, proportional under shortage)
replies.consolidationOff: Disabled consolidation. Each demand will plan its components independently. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.periodBucket: Set consolidation time bucket to **{days} day{plural}**. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.splitProportional: Set consolidation split policy to **proportional** — output is divided in proportion to each demand's requested quantity. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.splitPriority: Set consolidation split policy to **priority-first** — highest-priority demands are filled first from consolidated output. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.splitFair: Set consolidation split policy to **fair** — priority-first when supply is sufficient, proportional under shortage so no demand is starved. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.reset: Reset to defaults: by preference (cascade) method selection at depth 1, purchase disallowed, consolidation on (365-day bucket, fair split). Re-run plan to apply.
replies.help: I handle method selection, purchase, and shared-component consolidation. Try: "by preference", "elaborate method", "method depth 2", "equal split methods", "no purchase", "allow purchase", "enable consolidation", "set 14 day bucket", "proportional split", or "show config".
